## Exact statement and normalization
Given any finite simple graph G on n vertices, let R*(G) be the least N for which there exists a host graph H on N vertices such that ANY red-blue coloring of the EDGES of H contains a monochromatic copy of G which is also INDUCED by its vertex set in H. The conjecture is the UNIFORM exponential bound R*(G)<=2^(C*n) for an absolute constant C and all G; it is not asserting H=K_N, nor that G is a clique, nor that the induced embedding may add or omit host edges.

## Dated status and primary evidence
FROZEN 2025-09 catalogue: 'proved', though its reported 'Lean' formal solution label has NO admitted pinned formal statement; do not equate metadata with kernel receipt. Maintained Erdős #565 page, edited 2026-01-18, states PROVED and cites the independent existence solutions Deuber 1975, Erdős–Hajnal–Pósa 1975 and Rödl 1973, followed by earlier 2^O(n log² n) (Kohayakawa–Prömel–Rödl 1998), 2^O(n log n) (Conlon–Fox–Sudakov 2012).
MAIN SOURCE: Lucas Aragão, Marcelo Campos, Gabriel Dahia, Rafael Filipe, João Pedro Marciano, 'An exponential upper bound for induced Ramsey numbers', arXiv:2509.22629, original posted 2025-09-26 and revised 2025-11-13, https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22629. Their general theorem: there exists a universal C so R_ind(G;r)<=r^(C*r*n) for every G on n vertices, and integer r>=2. Setting r=2 yields 2^(2Cn), hence 2^O(n), solving the registered conjecture. Oxford 2025-10-14 seminar announcement by coauthor Marcelo Campos confirms the 2^O(n) statement. This is external source proof, not independently reconstructed or formally replayed by GCL.

## Strongest verified interface
Exact logical reduction: r^(C*r*n) at r=2 is 2^(2*C*n). Induction over colors is NOT needed for this specialization, but the quantifier over all G is essential. Exact independent small-graph fixture: R_ind(K3;2)=6. Since K6 is a Ramsey graph for two-color triangles, every 2-coloring has a monochromatic K3; an induced K3 in complete H is the same as an ordinary K3. Conversely any H on <=5 vertices can inherit a triangle-avoiding red/blue edge-coloring by restricting one of the 12 triangle-avoiding two-colorings of K5, so no H on <=5 vertices forces an induced monochromatic K3. An exhaustive direct checker counted 12 avoiding colorings on K5 and zero among 32,768 colorings on K6. This verifies a finite semantic instance, not the general induced theorem.

REPLAY: verify.py SHA256 25bfb6248b1bd96ceae6c7e600a923bcdd26bc37e289b94add4c1831b7dbc47a; 565.json SHA256 4385566d8d9da4dde211a0dfb3612f795a200ae99e61d146b1c4b3a6a5b35535. Recomputed locally in this task, not independently authenticated through CHAD.

## Proposed bounded successor task
At exact arXiv v2 source: capture theorem number and assumptions in full body, verify definition of induced Ramsey includes monochromatic edges of H and induced host adjacency (not induced colored subgraph only); prove the r=2 specialization and small exact K3 fixture above in Lean or independent symbolic method. Acceptance: precise universal constant quantifiers, allowance H to vary with G, and a complete trace showing all 2^15 colorings of K6 contain mono K3, with the K5 avoiding witness. Falsification: an induced embedding whose adjacency differs between H[vertices] and G, or a claimed source generalization dropping needed assumptions. Stop at source-fidelity; don't self-certify the complex external proof.

## Exact statement and normalization
For any finite simple undirected graph H with k vertices, let R_ind(H) be the smallest N for which there exists SOME host graph G on N vertices such that every 2-coloring of the host's EDGES contains a monochromatic copy of H that is induced as a graph in G. Erdős #565 asks whether a universal constant C>0 exists with R_ind(H)<=2^(Ck) for all H and k. An induced copy means induced relative to the underlying HOST graph, not a request that every edge or nonedge of a complete graph have the same color.

## Dated status and primary evidence
The pinned teorth/erdosproblems@536408716724a2402bdfa7c1d764bf83d64a8c89 catalogue entry 565 reports PROVED (2025-09-29) with no admitted formal proof. Primary research: L. Aragão, M. Campos, G. Dahia, R. Filipe, J. P. Marciano, *An exponential upper bound for induced Ramsey numbers*, arXiv:2509.22629v2 (2025-11-13), https://arxiv.org/html/2509.22629v2 ; Theorem 1.1 explicitly states an absolute C with R_ind(H)<=2^(Ck) for EVERY k-vertex H, the requested statement. Theorem 1.2 gives all r>=2 with R_ind(H;r)<=r^(Crk). The maintained https://www.erdosproblems.com/565 reports PROVED and attributes this paper. This evidence identifies an externally published/preprinted claimed proof, not a GCL-independent full mathematical verification.

## Strongest verified interface
Exact theorem-STATEMENT concordance: Theorem 1.1 uses a variable host graph, its order as the Ramsey quantity, 2-colorings of host edges, and host-induced monochromatic embeddings; all agree with the registered problem. Algebraically Theorem 1.2 at r=2 gives 2^(2Ck)=2^(C'k) with C'=2C, so there is no quantifier loss. Independently checked finite special case: R_ind(K3;2)=6, with 12 labeled 2-colorings of K5 avoiding monochromatic triangles and zero on K6. Script SHA-256 287412b2ded062755d83b339a32727c5e1dffbdebd4e12e0615868109f93241c; CHAD capture 0a9f60906dcb4b31a329730519190a17. Neither this fixture nor source citation amounts to a 59-page proof replay.

Separately formalize the induced-Ramsey definition and K3=6 fixture in pinned Lean/Mathlib, print axiom dependencies and source-locked CI receipt. Accept a local lemma only after no-sorry checking and mathematical review; do not require full preprint formalization for source-level citation acceptance.
